proof.text: The existing source-library theorems CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_isLimitFan and DerivedCategory.isLimitFanMkQObjOfIsKInjective construct products from K-injective representatives. proof.text: For the given strict filtered diagram C_i with common termwise bound a, step 1 identifies t^*(colim C_i) with colim t^*C_i by the original cocone. Both diagrams retain that termwise bound: an additive functor sends zero terms to zero. Apply the global-sections clause of lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity first on T and then on T_0 to the diagram t^*C_i. Both schemes are qcqs by hypothesis; the coefficient is the same arbitrary commutative condensed ring, and both diagrams and sites are small. Its common cohomological-bound hypothesis follows from the common termwise bound; the good truncation at a is canonically the original complex since the term in degree a-1 is zero. The cited theorem gives the two cocone-induced comparisons as quasi-isomorphisms of functorial bounded-below section representatives, independent of quasi-isomorphic replacements. Their Q-images are the two required isomorphisms in D(Ab).

proof.text: The existing functorial degreewise-injective K-injective replacement on a Grothendieck abelian category supplies a functorial monic injective embedding M -> I(M[0])^0: evaluate its monomorphic augmentation at degree zero. Apply the existing functorial bounded injective-resolution theorem on the source and target module categories. These replacements preserve every common termwise lower bound; their complexes are K-injective by Mathlib CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective. Taking sections of the first replacement defines P. Pull back that replacement, apply the target replacement, then take sections to define R. Underived section restriction followed by the second augmentation gives a natural chain transformation P -> R. The two-resolution formula of step 2 normalizes this transformation with the actual rho. The colimit complex has the same strict lower bound, since evaluation preserves colimits and a colimit of zero objects is zero. Evaluate the two functors and their chain transformation at this colimit and at its original cocone legs. Naturality gives the two normalized cocone equations and the commuting chain square. Step 6 gives the comparison isomorphisms for every normalized representative choice.

title: Actual closed restriction and derived products, triangles and bounded filtered colimits
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, and use the ordinary uncompleted derived categories and abelian-group-valued module-derived sections [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Sites and every indexing category are small in the fixed universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $t:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, with no quasi-compactness condition on its complementary open [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Identify $t^*\Lambda_T$ with $\Lambda_{T_0}$ by the canonical coefficient isomorphism. Define
$$\Phi(K)=R\Gamma(T,K),\qquad \Psi(K)=R\Gamma(T_0,t^*K),\qquad \rho_K:\Phi(K)\longrightarrow\Psi(K).$$
Here $t^*$ is the exact module inverse image, and $\rho$ is the actual derived restriction: on a complex resolve $K\to I$ by a K-injective complex on $T$, resolve $t^*I\to H$ by a K-injective complex on $T_0$, and use $\Gamma(T,I)\to\Gamma(T_0,t^*I)\to\Gamma(T_0,H)$, where the first arrow is section restriction from the pullback adjunction unit. These arrows specify the canonical derived transformation independently of the resolution choices.

The functors $\Phi,\Psi$ are additive and triangulated and $\rho$ commutes with their shift comparisons and is a morphism between their images of every distinguished triangle, including the connecting arrow [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For every small family $(K_i)$ the projection-induced comparisons
$$\Phi(\prod_iK_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i\Phi(K_i),\qquad\Psi(\prod_iK_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i\Psi(K_i)$$
are isomorphisms, and under these specified comparisons $\rho_{\prod_iK_i}=\prod_i\rho_{K_i}$ [def-weil-category-product]. For every strict small filtered diagram $(C_i^\bullet)$ of $\Lambda_T$-module complexes with one common termwise lower bound, put $C^\bullet=\varinjlim_iC_i^\bullet$. Then the cocone-induced comparisons
$$\varinjlim_i\Phi(QC_i^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi(QC^\bullet),\qquad\varinjlim_i\Psi(QC_i^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi(QC^\bullet)$$
are isomorphisms and identify $\varinjlim_i\rho_{QC_i^\bullet}$ with $\rho_{QC^\bullet}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The colimits here mean termwise filtered colimits of functorial bounded-below section-complex representatives; their value is independent of quasi-isomorphic replacements. No preservation of K-injectives by $t^*$ is assumed. No model, constructibility, rigidity, or coefficient-finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q37-bc89f4d5b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole split: the item (statement unchanged, 7 steps), the new statement-only node lem-sfb-exact-input-derived-transformation and the report, against HRS Lemma 5.3(1) and its proof, Stacks 09AA, and the full statement of every cited node. Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation applies with c=α_t, so t^* is exact and preserves products, and the sk-def adjunction makes it a left adjoint. Steps 3-4: products of abelian-group complexes are coordinatewise, lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective gives the product of K-injectives, and det-pe-products-derived applies on T and T_0. Together these show RΓ and D(t^*) preserve derived products without assuming t^* preserves K-injectives. Step 5 is naturality plus the product universal property. Step 6: a common termwise bound gives τ_{≥a}C_i=C_i because coker(0→C^a)=C^a, and the continuity node applies on both qcqs schemes, on T_0 to the diagram t^*C_i with colim t^*C_i=t^*C. Step 7: J(M)=I(M[0])^0 is a monic functorial injective embedding, because M→Z^0→H^0 is an isomorphism. With the functorial bounded injective resolution it gives a natural chain representative of ρ, and t^*C→I_0(t^*I(C)) is an admissible representative, so the colimit square commutes. New node: true. τ exists and is unique by the universal property in def-sfb-right-derived-functor, the two-resolution formula follows from naturality of η^G at j, and the shift equation from uniqueness. It is not a duplicate: lem-sfb-exact-square-right-derived-unit needs an invertible c, while β here is a non-invertible restriction; the other comparison nodes need an iso or K-injective preservation. The pinned Mathlib has no derived CommShift, so it is not a Mathlib leaf. It is generic and strictly smaller than the item. No cycle (closure walk of 814 nodes), proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, no SGA source. The nine declared tool_uses are generic infrastructure and are accepted. Advisory: the new node has no lean_audit key, as many new nodes on this base do.
